headline: KSE-100 clears 180,500 on energy-led buying as Wall Street slides, yields spike on Hormuz deadline lapse
mood: Risk-off abroad, energy-led gains at home · Hormuz is the swing factor

five_things.html: The benchmark closed Monday at 180,502.44, up 397.83 points (0.22%) from Thursday's 180,104.61 (PSX was shut Friday for Independence Day), on volume of 511.22m shares, as buying in oil & gas marketing, exploration and refinery names offset selling in banks, cement and fertilizer. Breadth was negative (43 advancers vs 57 decliners), so the headline gain was narrower than it looks. Sources: Business Recorder, Mettis Global.

five_things.chip: Wall Street slides as Hormuz deal lapses
five_things.html: The S&P 500 fell 40.70 points (0.5%) to 7,745.06, the Dow dropped 272.63 (0.5%) to 53,459.78 and the Nasdaq lost 84.25 (0.3%) to 26,644.91 after the 60-day US-Iran memorandum on the Strait of Hormuz expired without a successor deal and President Trump threatened action against Oman. Sources: AP via KVUE, Yahoo Finance.

The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.72% and the 2-year rose to 4.18%, while the 30-year surged past 5.31% — its highest level since 2007 — as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signalled a rate hike may not be his preferred inflation tool, and mounting government-debt concerns compounded the Hormuz-driven risk premium. Sources: CNBC, Trading Economics.

five_things.chip: Crude firms as Hormuz truce lapses
five_things.html: WTI jumped 3.09% to $84.95/bbl while Brent held near $88.31/bbl as the interim US-Iran ceasefire formally expired and talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remained deadlocked, even as covert crude flows through the waterway capped further gains. Sources: Trading Economics, CNBC.

Gold traded near $4,440/oz, up modestly after soft US retail sales data (−0.6% in July) trimmed rate-hike odds, while silver climbed 1.3% to $65.66/oz; both remain well off gold's 2026 record above $5,000 but supported by continued Chinese central-bank buying. Sources: Yahoo Finance, Trading Economics.

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's headline CPI eased to 9.2% y/y in July from 11.1% in June, still above the SBP's 5–7% target band, after the Monetary Policy Committee held the policy rate at 11.5% for a second straight meeting. The KSE-100's push through 180,500 on Monday was powered almost entirely by energy names riding firmer international crude, while banks and fertilizers lagged — breadth stayed negative (43 gainers vs 57 losers), a reminder the rally lacks broad participation. Attention now turns to September, when an IMF mission is expected in Islamabad for the fourth EFF/second RSF review that could unlock roughly $1.2bn, with energy-sector circular-debt reforms the key test.
matrix.gcc_html: Saudi Arabia's non-oil private sector stayed expansionary for a fourth straight month, with the Riyad Bank PMI easing only slightly to 53.1 in July from 53.3 in June, even as export orders fell for a fifth month on high freight costs. The PIF's newly published 2026–2030 strategy prioritises tourism, urban development, advanced manufacturing, logistics, clean energy and NEOM, alongside reporting strong FY2025 revenue and profit growth. The Hormuz standoff — the interim US-Iran memorandum expired Monday without a successor deal — is a near-term fiscal tailwind for Gulf exporters via firmer crude, even as it raises shipping and insurance-cost risk for the region.
matrix.global_html: Wall Street fell Monday — S&P 500 −0.5% to 7,745.06, Dow −0.5% to 53,459.78, Nasdaq −0.3% to 26,644.91 — after the 60-day US-Iran memorandum governing the Strait of Hormuz expired without a successor deal, President Trump threatened action against Oman, and a senior Iranian official floated an "offensive policy" if diplomacy fails. The 30-year Treasury yield surged past 5.31%, its highest since 2007, and the 10-year rose to 4.72% as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signalled a hike may not be his preferred tool against inflation, compounding debt-driven pressure on long yields. WTI jumped 3.1% to $84.95/bbl on the Hormuz risk premium, while gold held above $4,400/oz (silver $65.66, +1.3%) on softer US retail sales, both still well off 2026's record above $5,000.

legislative.policy_html: IMF fourth EFF / second RSF review preparations begin ahead of a September mission, focused on energy circular-debt targets; SBP holds policy rate at 11.5% as July CPI eases to 9.2%.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: exporters and energy-linked equities if the ~$1.2bn tranche clears, easing FX reserve pressure. Loses: banks and rate-sensitive sectors, which had priced in an earlier cut that the hold denies them.

legislative.policy_html: Saudi Arabia's new Copyright Law took effect August 12, modernising IP protection for digital/AI-era content; UAE's merger-control executive regulations took force July 30.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: content creators, rights holders and compliant multinationals gaining clearer IP and antitrust certainty. Loses: platforms and acquirers facing new compliance costs and longer merger-clearance timelines.

legislative.policy_html: The US-Iran interim Strait of Hormuz memorandum expired Monday without a successor deal; Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signals a hike may not be his preferred inflation tool even as long-dated yields hit multi-decade highs.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: energy producers and the dollar on the risk premium; Gulf exporters via firmer crude. Loses: rate-sensitive growth equities, EM borrowers facing costlier dollar funding, and shippers exposed to Hormuz transit risk.

levels.support_note: first floor below Monday's intraday low of 180,282; deeper support at 177,700
levels.resistance_note: Monday's intraday high; then round-number resistance at 182,000

desk_stance_html: We read Monday's KSE-100 move as narrow strength: the headline print flatters a session in which decliners outnumbered advancers 57 to 43, and the entire gain was concentrated in energy names tracking firmer WTI. That makes the tape vulnerable to a reversal if Hormuz tensions ease or profit-taking hits oil & gas counters. Offshore, a spiking long end of the US Treasury curve — the 30-year at a 19-year high — and an unresolved Hormuz standoff argue for caution on risk assets broadly, while Gulf non-oil momentum and Pakistan's improving inflation trajectory remain the more durable medium-term supports. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

linkedin_text:
KSE-100 clears 180,500 — but the breadth tells a different story

Good morning. Here's the Economic Vibes desk read for Tuesday, 18 August 2026.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
Wall Street fell Monday after the 60-day US-Iran memorandum governing the Strait of Hormuz expired without a successor deal and President Trump threatened action against Oman: S&P 500 -0.5% to 7,745.06, Dow -0.5% to 53,459.78, Nasdaq -0.3% to 26,644.91. The 30-year Treasury yield surged past 5.31% — its highest since 2007 — and the 10-year rose to 4.72% as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signalled a hike may not be his preferred tool against inflation.

PAKISTAN
KSE-100 closed at 180,502.44 (+397.83 pts, +0.22%) on volume of 511.22m shares, but breadth was negative — 43 gainers vs 57 losers. The rally was almost entirely energy-led (CNERGY, PSO, ATRL, SSGC) tracking firmer crude, while banks, cement and fertilizer lagged. July CPI eased to 9.2% y/y and SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a second straight meeting. An IMF mission is expected in September for the fourth EFF/second RSF review, which could unlock roughly $1.2bn.

GCC
Saudi non-oil PMI held near 53 in July, staying expansionary for a fourth straight month, and PIF published its 2026-2030 strategy prioritising tourism, urban development, manufacturing, logistics, clean energy and NEOM alongside strong FY2025 results. Firmer oil on the Hormuz standoff is a fiscal tailwind for exporters even as it raises regional shipping-cost risk.

GLOBAL
WTI jumped 3.1% to $84.95/bbl on the Hormuz risk premium while Brent held near $88.31/bbl. Gold held above $4,400 (silver $65.66, +1.3%) on softer US retail sales (-0.6% in July), though both remain well off 2026's record above $5,000.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: IMF fourth review prep + SBP rate hold — wins for exporters if the tranche clears, headwind for rate-sensitive banks.
• GCC: Saudi's new Copyright Law (Aug 12) and UAE's merger-control regulations (Jul 30) tighten IP and antitrust frameworks — wins for rights holders, added compliance cost for platforms and acquirers.
• Global: Hormuz memorandum lapses, Warsh signals hike may not be preferred tool — wins for energy and the dollar, headwind for rate-sensitive growth equities and EM borrowers.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 179,500 · pivot 180,502 (Monday's close) · resistance 181,159 (Monday's high), then 182,000. We read Monday's move as narrow strength — the entire gain was concentrated in energy names, and decliners outnumbered advancers. That leaves the tape vulnerable to a reversal if Hormuz tensions ease. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
